name: The million lives particle field
description: About 1,000 particles, each standing for 1,000 lives, drift gently in a field. As the cohort ages, particles fade out so that the visible count always equals round(1000 * lx / l0) from the engine. The field is a picture of the engine's numbers and must not calculate anything.

userStories.title: Particle field driven by survivor counts
userStories.description: src/particles.mjs exports createField(canvas, count) and update(field, aliveCount, dt). Particles have fixed positions and a slow drift; the field keeps exactly aliveCount particles visible, fading the others out over about 400 ms in a fixed order so the same age always shows the same picture.
acceptanceCriteria: At age 0, 1,000 particles are visible; at 121, none
The number of visible particles at every age equals round(1000 * lx / l0) from the engine (export a pure visibleCount(lx, l0) helper and test it in tests/particles.test.mjs)
Math.random is used only for initial positions and drift, never for which or how many particles are alive
The animation holds 60 fps on a 2020 laptop with 1,000 particles (use a single canvas, no DOM per particle)

userStories.title: Deaths fade, survivors drift
userStories.description: A particle that dies fades and shrinks over 400 ms. Living particles drift slowly with a subtle glow. Reset restores every particle instantly.
acceptanceCriteria: Playing from age 60 shows a visibly accelerating thinning of the field between ages 75 and 100
Reset shows all 1,000 particles within one frame
Pause freezes deaths but drift continues

technicalNotes.rationale: Canvas animation with one pure, testable helper.
